327695.title: Near-Hamiltonian cycle conjecture for minimal triangle-free $k$-chromatic graphs
327695.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic triangle-free graph, and let $n_k$ be the minimum number of vertices in a $k$-chromatic triangle-free graph. **Near-Hamiltonian cycle conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains a cycle of length at least

$$
n_k-o(n_k).
$$

This conjecture predicts that every $k$-chromatic triangle-free graph has a cycle covering all but a sublinear number of the vertices of a smallest $k$-chromatic triangle-free graph. The authors present it as a belief in the concluding remarks; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
327695.assessment: Asymptotic quantifier k→∞ and uniform little-o are essential; small chromatic endpoint examples are irrelevant. Need uniform long-cycle bound approaching extremal order, not a fixed proportion.

327714.title: Dimca's bound for the Griffiths–Dwork reduction index
327714.literal_statement:
Let $f$ be the polynomial defining the rational integral, and let $r_f$ denote the integer for which the reduction operation $[\,]_{r_f}$ has the properties established earlier in the paper. The paper explains that $r_f$ is explicit but difficult to compute, since Dimca's proof expresses it in terms of a resolution of the singularities of the projective variety $V(f)$. **Dimca's conjecture.** Dimca conjectured that

$$
r_f\leqslant n+1.
$$

This bound would provide an a priori termination bound for the reduction algorithm and avoid dependence on a resolution of the singularities. The source gives no evidence here that the conjecture has been resolved.
327714.assessment: Reduction index depends on actual singularity-resolution construction. No bound proved; need primary definition and uniform stabilization lemma, not termination for one polynomial.

327738.title: Cranston–Rabern's chromatic bound conjecture for vertex-transitive graphs
327738.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a vertex-transitive graph, with chromatic number $\chi(G)$, clique number $\omega(G)$, and maximum degree $\Delta(G)$. **Cranston–Rabern's conjecture.** Every vertex-transitive graph satisfies

$$
\chi(G) \leq \max \left\\{ \omega(G), \left\lceil\frac{5\Delta(G) + 3}{6}\right\rceil \right\\}.
$$

The conjecture is supported by the bounds and cases proved in the paper; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
327738.assessment: Universal vertex-transitive chromatic bound. No certificate found; clique blowups/cycles only recover standard test families. Requires new bound or explicit transitive finite violation.

327739.title: Cranston–Rabern's strong-coloring conjecture for vertex-transitive graphs
327739.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a vertex-transitive graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $s\chi(G)$ denote its strong chromatic number, the smallest $r$ such that every partition of $V(G)$ into parts of size $r$ admits a proper coloring using all $r$ colors on each part. **Cranston–Rabern's strong-coloring conjecture.** The strong chromatic number of any vertex-transitive graph is at most

$$
s\chi(G) \leq \frac52\Delta.
$$

This is introduced as an intermediate conjecture toward the strong $2\Delta$-colorability conjecture; the supplied source gives no resolution.
327739.assessment: Strong coloring quantifies over every equal-block partition, with padding conventions to restore from primary. Testing ordinary colorings cannot refute this. Parked before primary investment.

327765.title: Dependently rigid characterization of the maximum likelihood threshold
327765.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a graph. A framework $(G,P)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is **$n$-dependently rigid** if every edge-equivalent framework $(G,Q)$ in $\mathbb{R}^m$ has an affinely dependent set of points, and $G$ is generically $n$-dependently rigid if every generic framework $(G,P)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $n$-dependently rigid.

**Dependently rigidity conjecture.** The maximum likelihood threshold of $G$ is greater than $n$ if and only if $G$ is generically $n$-dependently rigid.

This conjecture is presented as a proposed connection between maximum likelihood thresholds and a stronger form of combinatorial rigidity. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
327765.assessment: Definition of dependent rigidity and ambient dimension m requires primary restoration. No generic-framework/MLT equivalence established; cannot replace genericity with one sample.

327769.title: Subgraph-closed classes with strongly sublinear separators have subexponential expansion
327769.literal_statement: Let ${\cal G}$ be a subgraph-closed class of graphs. Suppose that ${\cal G}$ has strongly sublinear separators. **Subexponential expansion conjecture.** The expansion of ${\cal G}$ is subexponential; that is, there exists a function $f$ with $\log f(k)=o(k)$ such that the expansion of ${\cal G}$ is bounded by $f$. This would remove the bounded-maximum-degree hypothesis from the paper's theorem and give an almost precise characterization of graph classes with sublinear separators in terms of subexponential expansion.
327769.assessment: Uniform graph-class separator-to-expansion theorem; bounded-degree case explicitly insufficient. No full-scope proof; later polynomial-expansion literature not cleared.

327818.title: Graver-basis edge-connectivity conjecture for fiber graphs
327818.literal_statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{d\times n}$ be an integer matrix with $\ker(A)\cap\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n=\{\mathbf{0}_n\}$. For each right-hand side, let the **Graver fiber graph** be the fiber graph whose edges are defined by the Graver basis of $A$; its edge-connectivity is the minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects the graph, and its minimal degree is the minimum vertex degree.

**Graver-basis edge-connectivity conjecture.** In all Graver fiber graphs of $A$, the edge-connectivity equals the minimal degree.

The source motivates this conjecture from results showing that Graver moves give strong edge-connectivity properties, while noting that the corresponding vertex-connectivity question is unresolved. The supplied text gives no resolution of this edge-connectivity conjecture.
327818.assessment: Read actual Graver definition, fiber setup, Theorem4 proof route and Conjecture3. Exact box-intermediate edge test derived; 623 bounded fibers checked with no counterexample. Conformal shortest paths alone do not supply degree-many edge-disjoint paths across arbitrary cuts. Next lemma: transport all neighbors of a minimal cross-cut pair to distinct cut edges without violating nonnegativity. Unproved.

327822.title: Positive Alon–Edelman conjecture for several power indices
327822.literal_statement: Let an Alon–Edelman type result mean a bound showing that a simple game's power vector is close to the power vector of a game with only the concentrated $k$ voters and the remaining voters as dummies. **Alon–Edelman positivity conjecture.** The nucleolus, the minimum sum representation index, the Shapley–Shubik index and, more generally, $p$-binomial semivalues are positive answers to the question of which power indices admit Alon–Edelman type results. The paper reports such results for some indices, but does not establish the full stated generality in the supplied passage.
327822.assessment: Compound claim about four inequivalent power indices and concentration constants. No single index definition restored, no uniform bound. A k-voter numerical example would not establish stated generality.

327841.title: Minimum-dimension conjecture for collapse-free Hecke algebras
327841.literal_statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system whose Coxeter diagram is the simply laced bipartite graph $G$. Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{q})$ be the Hecke algebra with independent parameters, and let $\mathcal I(G)$ denote the set of independent sets of $G$. **Minimum-dimension conjecture.** The minimum dimension of a collapse-free $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{q})$ is

$$
|\mathcal I(G)|,
$$

and this minimum is attained when $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{q})$ is commutative. Computations suggest this claim, and it is verified for Coxeter systems of type $A$; the general simply laced bipartite case remains open.
327841.assessment: Read collapse-free definition, Lemmas3.3/3.4/4.1, basis construction and 5.1–5.4 proofs. Independent-set→basis injection fails as a shortcut: domination annihilates a whole nonzero-parameter connected block even when only a different vertex of that block is chosen. Need a cardinality-preserving replacement for lost independent sets, uniformly on bipartite diagrams. No such injection proved.

327876.title: Hodge-theoretic determination of the Orlov spectrum
327876.literal_statement: Let $X$ be a Fano variety, let $M(\mathbb{P}^1, CY)$ be the zero fiber of the Stability Hodge Structure of $D^b(X)$, and let $\overline{M(\mathbb{P}^1, CY)}$ be its compactification with divisor at infinity $D$. For a point $p$ on a component of $D$, let $\widehat{\mathcal{O}}_p$ be the completion of the local ring at $p$. **Orlov-spectrum conjecture.** The mixed Hodge structures on the completions $\widehat{\mathcal{O}}_p$, as $p$ runs over all components of $D$, determine the Orlov spectrum of $D^b(X)$. This proposes a Hodge-theoretic interpretation of generation times and gaps in the Orlov spectrum; the source gives no resolution.
327876.assessment: Categorical/Hodge determination assertion lacks a tractable finite semantic bridge. No proof and no claimed formulation beyond literal record.

327884.title: Hirsch bound conjecture for the circuit diameter of polyhedra
327884.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be an $n$-dimensional polyhedron with $f$ facets. Its **circuit diameter** is the maximum number of maximum-length steps along circuit directions needed to go from one vertex of $P$ to another.

**Circuit diameter bound.** For any $n$-dimensional polyhedron with $f$ facets, the circuit diameter is bounded above by

$$
f-n.
$$

The circuit diameter is an analogue of the combinatorial diameter based on circuit directions and gives a lower bound on the number of augmentation steps under selection rules for linear programming. The analogous Hirsch bound for combinatorial diameter is false in general, so whether it always holds for circuit diameter is the question posed here.
327884.assessment: Circuit steps must be maximal and feasible; a non-Hirsch combinatorial diameter does not imply circuit violation. No explicit circuit certificate or general bound obtained.

327918.title: de Mier's symmetry conjecture for crossing and nesting numbers of linked partitions
327918.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $P$ be a linked partition of $[n]$. In its linear representation, arcs are pairs $(i,j)$ with $i<j$. A $k$-crossing consists of arcs satisfying

$$
i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k<j_1<j_2<\cdots<j_k,
$$

and a $k$-nesting consists of arcs satisfying

$$
i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k<j_k<\cdots<j_2<j_1.
$$

Let $\mathrm{cr}(P)$ and $\mathrm{ne}(P)$ be the largest sizes of a crossing and nesting, respectively. **de Mier's conjecture.** For any positive integers $i$ and $j$, the number of linked partitions $P$ of $[n]$ with $\mathrm{cr}(P)=i$ and $\mathrm{ne}(P)=j$ equals the number of linked partitions $P$ of $[n]$ with $\mathrm{cr}(P)=j$ and $\mathrm{ne}(P)=i$. The source says that de Mier had shown the case $i=1$ and that the authors prove the full symmetry.
327918.assessment: Literal itself says authors prove full symmetry. Exclude known-in-source; no claim of fresh resolution from open tag.

327965.title: The cycle extension distinguishing number conjecture
327965.literal_statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{ext}_D(C_n)$ denote the minimum number of blanks such that every coloring of the remaining vertices extends to a distinguishing coloring of $C_n$. 

**Cycle extension conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ext}_D(C_n)=\begin{cases}4&\text{if }n\not\equiv 0\pmod{4\text{ or }5},\\5&\text{if }n\equiv 0\pmod 4,\\6&\text{if }n\equiv 0\pmod 5.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture is sharp for the displayed cases, and the paper verifies it whenever the minimum prime divisor of $n$ is at least $7$; the general case remains open.
327965.assessment: Piecewise divisibility cases overlap at multiples20; cannot count wording repair or small-cycle exceptions. No general distinguishing extension mechanism proved.

327967.title: The plane extension distinguishing number conjecture
327967.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{R}^2$ be the Euclidean plane with its natural group action, and let $\operatorname{ext}_D(\mathbb{R}^2)$ denote its extension distinguishing number.

**Plane extension conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ext}_D(\mathbb{R}^2)=7.
$$

The value is motivated by lower bounds from faithful graph embeddings and by the relation between extension distinguishing numbers of spheres and Euclidean spaces; determining the exact value remains open.
327967.assessment: Full Euclidean isometry action and every precoloring matter. Finite dihedral witness gives only a lower bound; no seven-blank extension proof.

327972.title: Akbari et al.'s planar edge Roman domination conjecture
327972.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\gamma'_R(G)$ denote its edge Roman domination number: the minimum of $\sum_{e\in E(G)}f(e)$ over all functions $f\colon E(G)\to\{0,1,2\}$ such that every edge assigned $0$ is adjacent to an edge assigned $2$. **Akbari et al.'s conjecture.** If $G$ is planar, then

$$
\gamma'_R(G)\leq \frac{6}{7}n.
$$

This conjecture removes the claw-free hypothesis from the preceding planar bound. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture, so its status remains open.
327972.assessment: Planar edge Roman domination bound requires all planar graphs. No exact planar witness/certificate; matching or vertex domination replacement is not an equality of invariants.

327973.title: The large-girth planar edge Roman domination conjecture
327973.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $3k+2$ with $n$ vertices, and let $\gamma'_R(G)$ denote its edge Roman domination number: the minimum of $\sum_{e\in E(G)}f(e)$ over all functions $f\colon E(G)\to\{0,1,2\}$ such that every edge assigned $0$ is adjacent to an edge assigned $2$. **Large-girth planar conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar graph of girth at least $3k+2$ on $n$ vertices, then

$$
\gamma'_R(G)\leq \frac{2k+2}{3k+2}n.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by known bounds for planar graphs of specified girth, and its right-hand coefficient tends to $\frac{2}{3}$ as $k$ tends to infinity, reflecting the tree-like behavior of planar graphs with large girth. No resolution is supplied in the given text.
327973.assessment: All girth parameters k and all planar graphs; forests do not refute tending coefficient. Need uniform discharging or exact planar witness. None proved.

328018.title: Unique nondegenerate minimum conjecture for the magnetic wedge edge eigenvalue
328018.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha_{0}\in(0,\pi)$, and let $\mu^\mathsf{e}(s,\eta)$ denote the lowest eigenvalue of the Neumann realization of

$$
\mathcal{M}^{\mathsf{e}}_{s,\eta}=D_{t}^2+\mathcal{T}(s)^{-2}\mathcal{T}(0)^2D_{z}^2+(\eta-t)^2
$$

on the sector $\mathcal{S}_{\alpha_{0}}$. **Unique-minimum conjecture.** The function $\eta\mapsto\mu^\mathsf{e}(0,\eta)$ admits a unique critical point $\eta_{0}$, which is a nondegenerate minimum. This conjecture concerns the spectral behavior of the magnetic Neumann Laplacian near a varying edge; its status is not determined by the supplied source.
328018.assessment: Requires lowest Neumann spectral branch on every sector angle and unique nondegenerate critical point. Neither finite discretization nor numerical critical point proves full assertion.

328029.title: Mosaic number conjecture for the knots $6_{1}$ and $6_{3}$
328029.literal_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, an **$n$-mosaic** is an $n\times n$ mosaic-tile board representing a link or knot, and the **mosaic number** of a knot is the smallest natural number $m$ for which it has a knot $m$-mosaic. The knots $6_{1}$ and $6_{3}$ denote the standard six-crossing knots in knot tables. **Mosaic number conjecture for $6_{1}$ and $6_{3}$.**

$$
\text{The mosaic number of }6_{1}\text{ and }6_{3}\text{ is }6.
$$

The claim concerns the unresolved determination of mosaic numbers for knots with at most ten crossings; the source gives no evidence of a resolution.
328029.assessment: Two fixed knot types but mosaic equivalence needs Reidemeister/topological semantics and exhaustive lower obstruction. No new proof; later source cache exists historically but not reread here.

328045.title: The girth–minimum-degree lower-bound conjecture for zero forcing number
328045.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with girth $g geq 3$ and minimum degree $delta geq 2$.

**The girth–minimum-degree conjecture.**

$$
(g-3)(\delta - 2) + \delta \le Z(G).
$$

This conjecture proposes a lower bound for the zero-forcing number that grows with both the girth and the minimum degree. It is numerically verified for the triangle-free graphs in the stated database range and follows for sufficiently large minimum degree when $g>6$ from tree-width bounds, but remains open in general.
328045.assessment: Uniform zero forcing process and girth. No new full-scope lower bound; finite seed sweeps would not prove it. Later-literature scope not cleared.

328046.title: The triangle-free lower-bound conjecture for zero forcing number
328046.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph with minimum degree $delta geq 2$.

**Triangle-free zero-forcing conjecture.**

$$
2\delta -2 \leq Z(G).
$$

This is the $g=4$ specialization of the broader girth–minimum-degree conjecture and concerns improving the trivial minimum-degree lower bound for triangle-free graphs. The paper presents it as a conjecture analogous to its proved bounds, but does not establish it in general.
328046.assessment: Specialization of328045; even a proof cannot earn a separate family credit. No proof attempted beyond literal mechanism assessment.

328048.title: NP-completeness of induced cycle for cubic graphs
328048.literal_statement:
A **cubic graph** is a graph in which every vertex has degree $3$. The decision problem **INDUCED CYCLE** asks whether a graph has an induced cycle of the specified type considered in the paper.

**Cubic induced-cycle NP-completeness conjecture.** INDUCED CYCLE is NP-complete for cubic graphs.

The paper proves NP-completeness for graphs of maximum degree $4$ but conjectures the stronger result for cubic graphs; the source gives no resolution.
328048.assessment: Record omits precise specified induced-cycle type; cubic-graph NP-hardness needs source reduction and complexity semantics. Not a literal well-specified Lean target yet.

328054.title: Cahn–Levi–Kálmán minimal-genus conjecture for virtual Legendrian knots
328054.literal_statement: Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be Legendrian knots in the spherical cotangent bundle $ST^*M$ of a surface $M$. Suppose that they are isotopic as virtual Legendrian knots and that $M$ has the smallest genus among surfaces realizing knots in their virtual Legendrian isotopy class. **Minimal-genus conjecture.** Possibly after applying a contactomorphism of $ST^*M$, the knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ are Legendrian isotopic in $ST^*M$. The paper states that this conjecture, formulated by P. Cahn, A. Levi, and the first author, is solved by the stated corollary; the supplied parser nevertheless marks the conjecture as open, and that status is retained here.
328054.assessment: Literal states source corollary solves it. Exclude known-in-source; parser open status has no mathematical force.

328077.title: Tait's minimal alternating diagram conjecture
328077.literal_statement:
A link diagram is **alternating** when its crossings alternate between overcrossing and undercrossing along every component; an alternating link is one admitting a reduced alternating diagram. For such a link, crossing number is the minimum number of crossings among all diagrams representing it.

**Tait's conjecture.** Every alternating link has an alternating diagram with minimal crossing number among all diagrams of that link.

This is one of Tait's classical conjectures about alternating links and crossing number. It was proved for alternating links through work on the Jones polynomial and the Tait graph.
328077.assessment: Literal explicitly records classical proved Tait conjecture. Exclude known; formalization would not be a new result.

328167.title: Stable fluctuations for randomly biased walks on leafless Galton–Watson trees
328167.literal_statement: Consider randomly biased random walks on Galton–Watson trees without leaves, with exponent $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and assume a non-lattice condition. **Stable-fluctuation conjecture.** It would be interesting to determine whether stable fluctuations occur in this regime; this should hold only if no slowdown strong enough to break the central limit theorem can occur outside of pipes. The statement is conditional and exploratory, so its precise mathematical formulation remains to be established.
328167.assessment: Literal expressly says precise formulation remains to be established. No exact quantifiers/technical conditions to prove; cannot invent narrower conjecture.

328185.title: Maximum-rank stress conjecture for global rigidity on surfaces
328185.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be a surface, let $(G,p)$ be a framework generic on $S$, and let $(\omega,\lambda)$ be an equilibrium stress for $(G,p)$. Write $\Omega_S(\omega,\lambda)$ for its stress matrix, and let $\mu$ denote the dimension of the space of trivial infinitesimal motions on $S$. **Maximum-rank stress conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{rank} \Omega_S(\omega,\lambda)=3n-\mu,
$$

then $(G,p)$ is globally rigid on $S$. The preceding discussion establishes this when the stress matrix is positive semidefinite; the conjecture removes that positivity hypothesis.
328185.assessment: Surface, genericity and stress-matrix construction require primary restoration. Removing PSD not justified by rank alone without full rigidity argument. No result.

328198.title: The power-of-two conjecture for separating class sums of $W_n$
328198.literal_statement:
Let $W_n$ be the group considered above, and let a **separating set** be a collection of class sums whose eigenvalues distinguish the irreducible representations of the regular representation of $\mathbb{C}W_n$. **Power-of-two conjecture.** $W_n$ has a separating set consisting of $2^n$ class sums.

The conjecture is motivated by computed separating sets for $n\leq 4$ and by the recursive nature of the groups: the authors expect the smallest separating-set size for $W_{n+1}$ to be twice that for $W_n$. The computation only establishes an upper bound of $9$ for $W_4$, rather than the conjectured size $8$, and the general assertion remains open.
328198.assessment: Recursive group W_n not defined in record; count2^n and n=4 commentary have indexing tension. Do not count index repair; need actual group/central character definition.

328212.title: The BEL-gadget conjecture for 2-connected graphs
328212.literal_statement:
A **BEL gadget** is the graph-theoretic gadget used to establish computability of $s(H)$ for a graph $H$. The parameter $s(H)$ is the minimum degree among all Ramsey $H$-minimal graphs.

**BEL-gadget conjecture.** Every $2$-connected graph has BEL gadgets.

All $3$-connected graphs are known to have BEL gadgets, as do cycles and the graph $H_{t,2}$ considered in the paper. Whether every $2$-connected graph has a BEL gadget remains open.
328212.assessment: BEL gadget exact color-extension definition absent; no uniform gadget construction. Special cycles/3-connected cases already known according to literal.

328213.title: The linear upper-bound conjecture for minimum degrees of minimal Ramsey graphs
328213.literal_statement:
Let $s(H)$ denote the minimum degree among all Ramsey $H$-minimal graphs. Let $H$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta$ be its minimum degree.

**Linear upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
s(H)\leq \delta(n-1).
$$

The conjecture gives an upper bound for $s(H)$ in terms of the order and minimum degree of $H$, and the source notes that it is tight for both $K_k$ and $K_k\mathbin{\cdot}K_2$. Its general validity remains open.
328213.assessment: Uniform Ramsey-minimal construction needed for every connected H, preserving δ(n−1). No construction; standard clique instances uncredited.

328259.title: Gap-vector conjecture for Veronese embeddings
328259.literal_statement:
Let $X=v_d(\mathbb P^n)$ be the $d$th Veronese embedding of projective $n$-space, and define

$$
\bar j:=\min\{j:g_j(X)>0\}.
$$

Here $g_j(X)$ denotes the $j$th component of the gap vector of $X$, and $\operatorname{codim}X$ denotes the codimension of $X$. **Gap-vector conjecture.** The first nonzero component occurs at

$$
\bar j=\left\lceil\binom{n+d}{d}-(n+1)+\frac{1}{2}-\sqrt{\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+2\binom{n+2d}{2d}-2(n+1)\binom{n+d}{d}}\right\rceil,
$$

and, for $\bar j\leq j\leq\operatorname{codim}X$, one has

$$
g_j(X)=\binom{n+2d}{2d}-j(n+1)-\binom{\binom{n+d}{d}-j+1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the bounds previously established for the smallest index with positive gap are sharp, while also determining all subsequent components of the gap vector through codimension.
328259.assessment: Gap-vector definition required, especially no-positive-component cases. No generic interpolation or exact Gram-rank argument; endpoint low-degree issue alone ineligible.

328283.title: The manifold form of the cocompact action dimension conjecture
328283.literal_statement:
Let $(M,\partial M)$ be an $n$-manifold with contractible components that admits a geometric group action, and let $L^2H_i(M)$ denote its $L^2$-homology. **Manifold cocompact action dimension conjecture.**

$$
L^2H_i(M)=0\quad\text{for }i>n/2.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent manifold formulation of the cocompact action dimension conjecture, because a contractible $G$-manifold can be used to compute $L^2H_i(G)$. The source leaves the general assertion open.
328283.assessment: Manifold contractibility/action hypotheses and L2 homology must remain literal. No full vanishing theorem. Dropping contractibility to get sphere counterexamples is a wording correction, not valid research.

328299.title: AMP-UD recovery conjecture for stationary ergodic signals
328299.literal_statement: Consider a linear inverse problem in which an input signal ${\bf x}$, generated by a stationary ergodic source, is estimated from noisy measurements ${\bf y}$ and measurement matrix ${\bf A}$. AMP applies the proposed AMP-UD denoiser, based on context quantization and Gaussian-mixture-model-based i.i.d. subsequence denoising, within its iterations. **AMP-UD recovery conjecture.** Under some technical conditions, AMP-UD achieves the minimum mean-square error (MMSE). This is a more detailed formulation of the paper's AMP-UD conjecture; the result is presented without a proof, and the relevant technical conditions are not specified.
328299.assessment: Technical conditions explicitly unspecified. No exact universal AMP-UD endpoint available; cannot promote empirical recovery to MMSE theorem.

328365.title: The Bordeaux Conjecture of Borodin and Raspaud
328365.literal_statement: For a graph $G$, let $d^{\bigtriangledown}$ denote the minimum distance between distinct triangles of $G$. **Borodin and Raspaud's Bordeaux conjecture.** Every planar graph with $d^{\bigtriangledown}\geq 1$ and without $5$-cycles is $3$-colorable. This conjecture is presented as a planar graph 3-coloring problem related to the conjectures of Havel and Steinberg; the source does not provide evidence of resolution.
328365.assessment: Planarity, triangle distance and exclusion of5-cycles all essential. Steinberg counterexamples do not automatically satisfy this stronger triangle condition. No exact graph witness.

328367.title: The additive lower bound for m-eternal vertex cover
328367.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph, let $H$ be a subgraph of $G$, and let $G[V\setminus V(H)]$ be the subgraph induced by the vertices outside $H$. Write $\delta(\cdot)$ for minimum degree and let $\tau_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}$ denote the m-eternal vertex cover number. **The additive eternal vertex cover conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(H)\geq2\quad\text{and}\quad\delta(G[V\setminus V(H)])\geq2,
$$

then

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}(G)\geq\tau_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}(H)+\tau_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}(G[V\setminus V(H)]).
$$

The source presents this as an open conjecture in the eternal vertex-cover model.
328367.assessment: Full ordinary finite refutation and Lean endpoint completed. EXCLUDE_ROUTINE_COROLLARY: same authors2009Theorem4 and its shadow-guard proof supply upper bound immediately. Zero accepted credit despite correctness.
328367.semantic_limit: Closed-family safety-game semantics; forward infinite-play bridge proved in Lean. Converse to a separate history-dependent strategy datatype explained mathematically, not a separately formalized equivalence theorem. Excluded candidate only.

328376.title: Leydold's conjecture on maximal nodal domains of spherical harmonics
328376.literal_statement:
Let $\cal H_\ell$ be the eigenspace of spherical harmonics of degree $\ell$ on the sphere, and let $\mu(u)$ denote the number of nodal domains of a spherical harmonic $u$. **Leydold's conjecture.**

$$
\max_{u\in \mathcal H_\ell}\mu(u)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}\frac{1}{2}(\ell+1)^2 & \text{if }\ell\text{ is odd},\\[4pt]\frac{1}{2}\ell(\ell+2) & \text{if }\ell\text{ is even.}\end{array}\right.
$$

The right-hand side is attained by decomposed spherical harmonics in spherical coordinates. The conjecture was proved for $\ell\leq 6$, but remains open in general; it would determine all possible maximal nodal-domain counts and has consequences for Courant-sharp eigenvalues and Pleijel-type bounds.
328376.assessment: Degree0 discrepancy is only endpoint correction. Full nodal-domain maximization for arbitrary degree not established; no topological bound certificate.

328389.title: The regular simplex maximization conjecture for minimum projective distance
328389.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf{u}_0,\dots,\mathbf{u}_n$ be unit vectors representing the vertices of a simplex in complex projective space, in general position, and let

$$
D=|\det(\mathbf{u}_0,\dots,\mathbf{u}_n)|.
$$

Let $d_{\min}$ denote the minimum of the projective distances from the vertices to their opposite hyperplanes. Fix $0<D\leq 1$ and consider all configurations with this value of $D$. **Regular simplex conjecture.** Among all such configurations, the configuration with the largest $d_{\min}$ will be a regular simplex. The preceding theorem gives the bound $d_{\min}^n\leq D$, while equality of the relevant distances alone is not sufficient for equality; the conjecture identifies the regular simplex as the optimizer under fixed determinant magnitude.
328389.assessment: Full ordinary Gram/spectral optimizer argument in PROJECTIVE-328389.md. Key scalar minimization found explicitly in Aliyev2024 primary proof; strong routine-corollary objection. No Lean endpoint; zero credit.

328415.title: The GDN critical exponent and the index of primitivity
328415.literal_statement:
Let $CE_n$ denote the critical exponent for $n$-by-$n$ generalized doubly nonnegative matrices, and let $MIP_n$ be the maximum index of primitivity among primitive $n$-by-$n$ generalized doubly nonnegative matrices. **GDN critical exponent conjecture.**

$$
MIP_n-1<CE_n.
$$

The conjecture concerns the relationship between the largest index of primitivity and the critical exponent for generalized doubly nonnegative matrices. The preceding discussion motivates it by arguing that equality or the reverse inequality would require an unlikely multiple root in an associated exponential polynomial; no resolution is given in the source.
328415.assessment: Read GDN definition and section4 actual proof bodies. Lemma4.3 plus Proposition4.4 force MIP3=3; Corollary4.5 gives CE3=2, contradicting strict Conjecture4.1 in dimension3. This is a same-source parameter/strict-endpoint inconsistency, excluded by policy, not a new significant refutation. Generic derivative heuristic only gives non-strict bound; no larger-dimension full result.

328458.title: The giant component size conjecture in the Waiter–Client game
328458.literal_statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal L(n,q)$ denote the largest component size that Waiter can force in Client's graph when playing a $(q:1)$ Waiter–Client game on $E(K_n)$. **Giant component size conjecture.** For any constant $\varepsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, if $q=(1-\varepsilon)n$, then

$$
\mathcal L(n,q)=\min\{n,2(n-q-1)\}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the sharp value of the largest component in the supercritical regime. The paper proves a lower bound of $2\varepsilon n-2$ for the largest component when $q\leq(1-\varepsilon)n$, and the authors believe that the bound in the corresponding theorem is sharp.
328458.assessment: Exact minimax component size for sufficiently large n at fixed epsilon. Rounding/nonintegral bias is ineligible wording issue. No full game strategy or counterstrategy found.

328474.title: Snowden's uniform bounded-generation conjecture for GIT quotients
328474.literal_statement: Let $V$ be the vector space underlying the projective variety $\mathbb{P}(V)$, let $G$ be a linearly reductive group, and let $X$ be a $G$-polarized projective variety. For the invariant ring $R(n;m)$ associated with the quotient $\mathbb{P}(V)^m /\!/ \operatorname{PO}(V)$, write $d_0(n)$ and $d_1(n)$ for bounds depending only on $n$. **Snowden's conjecture.** There is a bound $d_0(n)$ such that $R(n;m)$ is generated in degree at most $d_0(n)$ for every $m$. After choosing a minimal set of generators, each of degree at most $d_0(n)$, there is a bound $d_1(n)$ such that the ideal of relations is generated in degree at most $d_1(n)$ for every $m$. The same assertion applies to every GIT quotient of the form $X^m /\!/ G$ with $G$ linearly reductive and $X$ a $G$-polarized projective variety. The conjecture would give bounds independent of the number of factors $m$. In the case considered here, the authors were unable to prove or disprove it; generation of the second Veronese subring in lowest degree gives limited evidence for its first part, while the proposition above gives partial progress toward an $m$-independent relation-degree bound for that Veronese subring.
328474.assessment: Uniform generator AND relation degrees for every factor count, further arbitrary polarizedGIT varieties. No bounded presentation theorem; special Veronese evidence insufficient.

328494.title: Doubly-exponential computability of the minimum variable-degree function
328494.literal_statement: Let $\operatorname{minnonmer}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ denote the minimum variable-degree function for minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets indexed by deficiency, and let $\operatorname{potprec}(\vec a)$ denote the functions represented by finite tuples $\vec a$. **Computability conjecture.** The function $\operatorname{minnonmer}$ is complex, is not equal to $\operatorname{potprec}(\vec a)$ for any finite tuple $\vec a$, and is nevertheless computable in doubly-exponential time. The paper presents this as a conjectural picture following its discussion of improved upper bounds.
328494.assessment: minnonmer/potprec definitions absent and complexity conjunction global. No double-exponential algorithm or separation; finite function values insufficient.

328505.title: Ore's recurrence conjecture for the minimum size of critical graphs
328505.literal_statement:
Let $f_k(n)$ be the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph, where a graph is $k$-critical if it is not $(k-1)$-colorable but every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable. **Ore's conjecture.** If $k\geq 4$, $n\geq k$, and $n\neq k+1$, then

$$
f_k(n+k-1)=f_k(n)+\frac{(k-2)(k+1)}{2}.
$$

Ore believed that repeatedly applying DHGO-composition with $K_k$ was best possible for constructing sparse critical graphs, which motivates this recurrence. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture, so its status remains open.
328505.assessment: Uniform critical-graph edge recurrence across all admissible orders. Known lower-edge bounds alone do not identify both minima for all residues. No new construction or exact counterexample.
